title: Lunar crewed rover environment, mobility, thermal and endurance audit for OTA-TEC-0036
question: Source-grounded audit of the exact OTA-TEC-0036 document. Using primary, peer-reviewed and official lunar mission/engineering sources, assess the real and hypothetical claims relevant to a pressurized early-colony lunar rover: (1) low-gravity traction, wheel-soil interaction, bounce/slide and rollover/stability evidence from Apollo LRV and modern lunar rover work; (2) lunar dust abrasion, electrostatic charging and effects on seals, joints, radiators and solar surfaces; (3) thermal management in vacuum, explicitly checking whether the dossier's statement that electronics reject heat 'exclusively by radiation' is too categorical and distinguishing internal conduction/transport from final external rejection; (4) representative lunar surface temperature ranges versus vehicle component exposure; (5) battery performance and thermal control in lunar cold; and (6) engineering plausibility/constraints for a 2–4 person pressurized rover with multi-hour to multi-day missions, including life-support and power/range reserve logic. Identify any wording in the source document that should be narrowed or reclassified. Do NOT evaluate or rewrite [F] build time, [F] 15–20 km/h gameplay/fiction choices, colony population/balancing values, Mars Credits, unlocks, journeys or any other NOXIA balancing value.
why_now: OTA-TEC-0036 is a new canonical NOXIA technical object with several real-world lunar engineering assertions and explicit [H] endurance/pressurization assumptions that should be audited before downstream game mappings harden.
real_world_anchor: Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicle operations, lunar dust and electrostatics, lunar thermal environment, batteries and pressurized crewed lunar rover engineering.
novelty_reason: First source-pinned evidence audit of the canonical NOXIA lunar rover object.
